schema_note: meanings by culture; source_keys without prefix -> semiotics/sources.json, 'culture:' prefix -> culture/sources.json; restriction: none|respect|legal; test_status always 'untested' until a comprehension test (see README section 5) is logged

meanings.thai: The Buddha himself, object of veneration; kept above head height; shoes off in its chapel.
meanings.western: Often read as generic 'zen / calm / spa / Asian decor'.
meanings.east_asian: Buddha in Mahayana traditions; also venerated.

risks_misreadings: Using it as decor, spa mood or product background offends many Thais
Buddha heads/cropped bodies, tattoos, on floors/toilets/bars = documented controversies
Penal Code s.206 covers acts against religious objects/places
use_for: Respectful documentary of temple visits (shot from below/level, nothing placed above it)
avoid: Any ad, product shot, meme, cartoon Buddha, cropped head, placing Buddha below feet or next to alcohol/sexualised content
symbols.evidence_note: Press + law text + etiquette guides agree; no audience study.

meanings.thai: Sangha, merit, morality; monks are revered and bound by Vinaya rules.
meanings.western: Exotic serenity, mindfulness; sometimes costume humour.
meanings.east_asian: Monks in Chinese/Japanese/Korean Buddhism wear other colours; similar reverence.

risks_misreadings: Costume monks, monks selling products, revered monks' faces on goods (Supreme case 2021)
Penal Code s.208: wrongfully using monk dress/symbols to deceive
use_for: Real merit-making scenes with consent; faceless silhouettes for culture explainers
avoid: Monk characters endorsing products, comic monks, AI-generated 'monk' selling eyewear
symbols.evidence_note: Law text + one enforcement case.

symbols.symbol: Sak yant / yantra designs, Buddha tattoos

meanings.thai: Protective sacred designs blessed by monks/ajarn; Buddha tattoos considered disrespectful by authorities.

risks_misreadings: Private campaign group Knowing Buddha runs billboards against Buddha tattoos/decor for tourists
Yant designs may be copyright-protected (DIP comment in Supreme case)
use_for: Explained cultural content with practitioners' consent
avoid: Decorative yant patterns on product graphics or merch
symbols.evidence_note: Press reports via search summary.

meanings.thai: Sacred space; shoes off in chapel; threshold not stepped on (guardian spirit); dress modestly.
meanings.east_asian: Temples - also sacred.

risks_misreadings: Fashion/product shoots in temples can read as using sacred space for sale
Stepping on thresholds, pointing feet at images
avoid: Sexualised poses, product placement on altars, drone shots over ceremonies without permission
symbols.evidence_note: Etiquette guide + law.

symbols.symbol: Chofa finial, naga bargeboards, gilded gable motifs

meanings.thai: Temple identity; chofa often read as Garuda or Hamsa; naga on roof edges and stair rails as guardians.

risks_misreadings: Lifting sacred architectural motifs into logos or packaging can look like appropriation of temple identity
use_for: Abstracted, clearly secular Thai patterns (kanok-style lines) with care
avoid: Exact chofa/naga temple elements on discount graphics
symbols.evidence_note: Chofa symbolism mainly from dealer/Wikipedia pages (weak).

meanings.thai: Purity, transcendence, faith; merit-making offering; Buddha seated on lotus; also used at funerals.
meanings.east_asian: Buddhist purity (China, Japan, Korea); purity rising from mud.

risks_misreadings: Funeral association in some Thai contexts (lotus in hands of the deceased)
Lotus under feet / on floor mats can feel disrespectful
avoid: Comic contexts, on shoes/floor, with alcohol
symbols.evidence_note: Museum page read (purity, spontaneous generation, faithfulness, awakening); Thai funeral/merit uses from Thai press via search summary only.

meanings.thai: National mythical creature (2025 designation); guardian of the Buddha and protector of waters, bringer of rain; temple stair-rail/roof guardian; fertility, wealth, abundance; Nong Khai naga fireballs; rival of Garuda.
meanings.east_asian: Chinese dragon/water deities (different creature).

risks_misreadings: Western viewers may read a serpent as threatening
Cartoon nagas for sales can offend believers
use_for: Water, rain, protection themes in Thai-only folklore stories
avoid: Mascot use for promotions
symbols.evidence_note: Thailex naga entry and The Nation (both read in full); academic folklore papers not read.

meanings.thai: Emblem of the state and monarchy; royal warrant mark granted to selected companies.
meanings.western: Eagle-like mythical bird; may be read as decorative.
meanings.east_asian: Garuda also in Indonesia (national emblem) and Hindu myth.

risks_misreadings: Khrut Pha Emblem Act B.E. 2534 as amended 2535: 'khrut pha emblem' = any garuda image in any pose, with or without text; using it (or a warrant-of-appointment emblem) without right so as to make others believe you have the right - up to 1 year and/or 6,000 baht (s.13)
Warrants are granted by royal charter via the Bureau of the Royal Household; using it implies royal endorsement
use_for: Never - unless a client legally holds the warrant and provides official artwork
avoid: Any Garuda drawing in logos, merch, posts
symbols.evidence_note: Act text (Wikisource translation) read in full; Wissanu 2021 statement read in full.

symbols.symbol: Royal portraits, royal family images, royal crests

meanings.thai: Deep respect; displayed in homes/shops; banknotes carry the King's portrait.

risks_misreadings: Penal Code s.112 (lèse-majesté): defame/insult/threaten King, Queen, Heir, Regent - severe prison terms
Anything placed above/over, edited, cropped, memed, or juxtaposed with products is high risk
Stepping on banknotes (King's image) is taboo per etiquette guides
use_for: Only official royal-occasion notices in the exact style the shop uses (e.g., closure/mourning), with untouched official imagery
avoid: Any creative edit, humour, AI-generated royal likeness, product next to royal image, royal colours as sales hook
symbols.evidence_note: Law text; current penalty 3-15 years per press summaries.

meanings.thai: Nation-Religion-King (red/white/blue as commonly taught); respect at 08:00/18:00 anthem.

risks_misreadings: Penal Code s.118 (current text): any act against a flag or other symbol of the State to desecrate the nation - up to 2 years and/or 40,000 baht; s.135 same for flags of friendly foreign states; Flag Act B.E. 2522 s.54 also criminalises flag desecration (text not read)
Flag on shoes, floors, trash, wipes
avoid: Distorted, cropped-as-pattern, or stepped-on flags
symbols.evidence_note: Penal Code ss.118/135 verified (1956 translation + current consolidated Thai text); Flag Act s.54 existence via Chula Law Journal 2024 abstract; colour meaning common teaching (unsourced).

meanings.thai: Royal sovereignty and prestige; historically royal possession.
meanings.western: Idiom 'white elephant' = costly useless burden (English idiom - unsourced here).

risks_misreadings: English idiom gives the opposite connotation to foreign viewers
Royal link makes jokey use risky
avoid: Product metaphors ('our white elephant deal')
symbols.evidence_note: Thai side sourced; English idiom common knowledge, unsourced.

meanings.thai: National animal (2025 Royal Gazette designation); strength, endurance, royal/war history; National Elephant Day 13 Mar (unsourced here).
meanings.western: Wisdom, memory, gentle giant; 'elephant in the room'.
meanings.east_asian: Strength; Ganesha (India) = remover of obstacles.

risks_misreadings: Elephant rides/performances raise animal-welfare backlash with foreign audiences (craft knowledge, unsourced)
Tourist cliché overuse
use_for: Pride, memory, steadiness metaphors; national day greetings
avoid: Riding/chain imagery; elephants as cheap 'Thailand' shorthand
symbols.evidence_note: One of six national symbols announced in the Royal Gazette on 14 May 2025 (The Nation, read in full). Welfare risk is unsourced craft.

meanings.thai: National flower (2025 designation); yellow blooms = unity, loyalty, prosperity (The Nation).

risks_misreadings: Yellow also carries royal/political associations - check timing
avoid: Political-season use
symbols.evidence_note: One of six national symbols announced in the Royal Gazette on 14 May 2025 (The Nation, read in full).

meanings.thai: National architecture symbol; rest, hospitality, Thai identity.

risks_misreadings: Low risk
symbols.evidence_note: One of six national symbols announced in the Royal Gazette on 14 May 2025 (The Nation, read in full).

symbols.symbol: Siamese fighting fish / Thai betta (pla kat)

meanings.thai: National aquatic animal (2025 designation); bravery and elegance (The Nation).

risks_misreadings: Fighting connotation; animal welfare in fish fights
avoid: Fight imagery
symbols.evidence_note: One of six national symbols announced in the Royal Gazette on 14 May 2025 (The Nation, read in full).

meanings.thai: Home/land guardian; daily offerings. Roots per Wannavithyapa 2026 abstract: guardian-deity belief (Buddhist suttas) + sacred space from ancestor/leader burial sites; Buddhism recast the guardian spirit as a deity in a palace; syncretism for coexistence.
meanings.east_asian: Chinese ancestor/earth-god shrines (possible origin, disputed).

risks_misreadings: Mocking, kicking, using as prop; showing it neglected may read as bad omen
avoid: Comic slapstick near shrine
symbols.evidence_note: Academic article abstract read; origin debate (Chinese shrine vs Brahmic) from search summary.

meanings.thai: Shop luck: beckons customers and money; kept by registers.
meanings.east_asian: Compare maneki-neko (Japanese beckoning cat) - similar commercial role.

risks_misreadings: Using a sacred-ish figure as sale mascot may feel cheap to believers
Beckoning gesture direction differs by culture
avoid: Cartoon Nang Kwak pushing discounts
symbols.evidence_note: Lexicon summary; origin uncertain.

meanings.thai: Blessing/protection; wedding binding; animist + Buddhist roots; wrist strings after blessings.
meanings.east_asian: Also Cambodia, Myanmar, Laos.

risks_misreadings: Low risk if shown in real ritual context
avoid: Cutting/throwing away string as a gag
symbols.evidence_note: Lexicon summary.

meanings.thai: Auspicious: homophone with 'step forward/progress'; nine monks at blessings; nine desserts; lucky plates sell for millions.
meanings.east_asian: Japanese 'ku' can sound like 'suffering' (general knowledge, unverified here); Chinese 9 ~ 'long-lasting' (unverified).

risks_misreadings: Japanese viewers may not share the positive reading
use_for: Thai promos: 9.9, 99, 'ก้าวหน้า' wordplay
symbols.evidence_note: One academic article (text garbled) + strong popular evidence.

meanings.thai: Neutral in Thai (no strong taboo found this session).
meanings.east_asian: Unlucky in Chinese, Japanese, Korean: 'four' ~ 'death'; floors labelled F or skipped; Chinese prices avoid 4.

risks_misreadings: Price endings, room numbers, '4 for 1' bundles for Chinese/Korean/Japanese customers
avoid: Tourist-facing prices ending in 4, '4-piece gift set' for Chinese buyers
symbols.evidence_note: Practice well documented; health effects contested.

meanings.thai: Neutral-positive (Chinese-Thai communities share Chinese reading).
meanings.east_asian: Chinese: prosperity ('ba' ~ 'fa'); price endings in 8 common in Chinese/Singapore ads.

risks_misreadings: Over-use looks like a gimmick to Western viewers
use_for: Chinese New Year promos, prices ending 88
symbols.evidence_note: Several price-ending studies.

meanings.thai: Not traditionally significant.

risks_misreadings: Minor; a few Western viewers notice
symbols.evidence_note: Unsourced common knowledge; Smith 2002 BMJ tested day 13 deaths (null) - see Phillips2001_BMJ limitations.

meanings.thai: Greeting, thanks, apology, respect; height/depth depends on status; junior initiates; deeper for monks/Buddha. Designated national cultural gesture (Royal Gazette, 14 May 2025).
meanings.western: Namaste/prayer-hands or 'thank you'; sometimes misread as prayer.

risks_misreadings: Wrong hierarchy (senior wai-ing junior first) looks odd; foreigners over-wai service staff
Wai with objects in hand, or as a jokey 'please buy'
use_for: Thank-you posts, apology notices, staff greeting customers
avoid: Mascots wai-ing products; mocking exaggerated wai
symbols.evidence_note: Etiquette guides consistent.

symbols.symbol: Touching someone's head / objects over heads

meanings.thai: Head most sacred; touching (even children's) or passing objects over heads is offensive.
meanings.east_asian: Also sensitive in parts of Asia.

risks_misreadings: Western 'pat on head' gesture reads as disrespect in Thailand
avoid: Scenes where an adult pats a Thai child/elder; product held over a person's head
symbols.evidence_note: Consistent guides.

symbols.symbol: Feet / soles pointing, feet on tables

meanings.thai: Feet lowest and least clean: don't point soles at people or Buddha images; don't move things with feet; don't step over pillows/books/food.
meanings.east_asian: Feet also impolite in much of Asia and Middle East (general).

risks_misreadings: Relaxed 'feet on desk' lifestyle shot is rude to Thai viewers
avoid: Feet toward camera/Buddha, shoes on table, pointing with foot
symbols.evidence_note: Consistent guides.

meanings.thai: Rude/accusatory toward people; prefer open hand or chin/lip gesture.
meanings.east_asian: Impolite in several Asian contexts (general).

risks_misreadings: Character pointing at customer reads accusatory
avoid: Pointing at people, at Buddha images
symbols.evidence_note: Cultural Atlas.

meanings.thai: Palm-down, fingers curled toward self; palm-up finger curl is offensive (used for animals).
meanings.east_asian: Palm-down beckon common in East/Southeast Asia (general).

risks_misreadings: Western palm-up beckon offends Thais; Thai palm-down beckon can look like 'go away' to Westerners
avoid: Palm-up beckon
symbols.evidence_note: Guides + emblem research shows form/meaning varies.

meanings.thai: Understood as OK by many (borrowed).
meanings.east_asian: 'Money' is one documented meaning of the ring (Matsumoto & Hwang; region not stated in the summary read).

risks_misreadings: Obscene in many European cultures (Maricopa); Brazil 'obscene' is a common claim not found in the sources read
Same form, different meanings: A-OK / money / other (Matsumoto & Hwang)
Co-opted by some hate groups online (unsourced here)
avoid: Mixed-audience ads relying on the gesture
symbols.evidence_note: Emblem study + textbook.

meanings.thai: Generally understood as 'good' (borrowed from global media).
meanings.other: Greece and other countries: insult 'Up yours!' (Maricopa citing Cotton 2013)

risks_misreadings: Insulting in Greece and some other countries
In VR command study, Chinese users preferred OK sign to confirm
avoid: Tourist-facing ads as the main message
symbols.evidence_note: Textbook claim; country list incomplete.

meanings.thai: Cute photo pose (very common in Thai selfies).
meanings.east_asian: Common cute photo pose (Japan, Korea, China).

risks_misreadings: Palm-inward version offensive in UK/Commonwealth
avoid: Palm-inward
symbols.evidence_note: Unsourced common knowledge - verify before relying.

meanings.thai: Smile can mask awkwardness/sadness/apology; nod = 'I hear you', not agreement.

risks_misreadings: Foreign viewers may misread a Thai character's apologetic smile as indifference
use_for: Subtle emotion in Mint & Tao via context
avoid: Captioning a smile as 'happy' without context
symbols.evidence_note: Cultural Atlas; see emotions/README section 2.10 on face reading.

meanings.thai: Neutral for most Thais (Chinese-Thai families may share taboo).
meanings.east_asian: Chinese: 'give a clock' ~ 'attend a deathbed/funeral' - wish of death, esp. to elders.

risks_misreadings: Watch/clock gift promos for Chinese customers
avoid: 'Gift a clock' campaigns for Chinese New Year
symbols.evidence_note: Newspaper explainer.

meanings.thai: Neutral.
meanings.east_asian: Chinese: 'umbrella' ~ 'separate' - bad for couples/friends.

risks_misreadings: Couples promos for Chinese buyers
avoid: Free umbrella with couple's purchase for Chinese market
symbols.evidence_note: Newspaper explainer.

meanings.thai: Generally neutral/decorative.
meanings.western: Autumn, cheer (US); funerals in parts of Europe (unsourced).
meanings.east_asian: China/Korea/Japan: funeral flower (white); also Japanese imperial crest (yellow 16-petal, unsourced).

risks_misreadings: Giving chrysanthemums = funeral connotation for Chinese viewers
avoid: Chrysanthemum bouquets as gift imagery for Chinese/Korean audiences
symbols.evidence_note: Gift-avoid lists; imperial crest unsourced.

meanings.thai: Some Thais also avoid writing names in red (unverified).
meanings.east_asian: Korea: writing a living person's name in red is taboo (death records/wreaths); seal stamps exempt; similar beliefs elsewhere in East Asia (unverified).

risks_misreadings: Red customer names in thank-you graphics, winner announcements
avoid: Korean (and East Asian) customer names in red
symbols.evidence_note: Volunteer-reporter article; Thai practice unverified.

meanings.thai: Neutral (feet low - giving shoes to elders may feel odd, unsourced).
meanings.east_asian: Korea: recipient will 'run away'; China: on avoid lists.

avoid: Couple-gift shoe promos for Korean audiences
symbols.evidence_note: Folk-belief reporting.

meanings.thai: Seen on some Buddhist/Hindu items; auspicious.
meanings.western: Nazi hate symbol (dominant reading since WWII).
meanings.east_asian: Japan: manji marks temples on maps; Hindu/Buddhist/Jain auspicious sign.

risks_misreadings: Western viewers read Nazism instantly regardless of orientation or context
avoid: Any decorative use; even incidental in temple backgrounds for foreign audiences - crop or explain
symbols.evidence_note: Encyclopedia + ADL agree.

meanings.thai: Chinese-Thai: auspicious (Chinese New Year, Yaowarat); naga is a separate Thai creature.
meanings.western: Menace, chaos, evil (Revelation); also heroic fantasy pets in modern media.
meanings.east_asian: China ('loong'): good luck, power, wealth, wisdom, harmony with nature; rain and harvests; 'descendants of the dragon'.

risks_misreadings: Aggressive dragon art for Western viewers; Western 'slay the dragon' metaphors for Chinese viewers
use_for: Chinese New Year promos with friendly, dancing dragons
avoid: Dragon as villain in content aimed at Chinese customers
symbols.evidence_note: CGTN article read in full (state media; expert quotes, no perception study).

symbols.symbol: Light vs dark skin as before/after or status cue

meanings.thai: Fair skin long associated with beauty/status in Thai advertising - and now a backlash trigger (colourism).
meanings.east_asian: Fair-skin ideal common, increasingly criticised.

risks_misreadings: Seoul Secret 2016 'white makes you a winner' ad pulled after outcry
avoid: Darkening/lightening skin to show 'better', winners lighter than losers, filters that whiten faces
symbols.evidence_note: Case + content analysis.

meanings.thai: Light = wisdom/merit (Buddhist 'light of Dhamma'), clarity; Loy Krathong/candles (unsourced).
meanings.east_asian: Similar broad pattern.

risks_misreadings: Broadly shared, but specific colour/lamp meanings vary
avoid: Assuming 'universal archetype' means no test is needed
symbols.evidence_note: Archetype evidence weak; light-dark is a common experience-based metaphor.

meanings.thai: Very strong: head high, feet low; Buddha and royalty placed highest; elders' heads not looked down on.
meanings.east_asian: Similar.

risks_misreadings: In Thailand vertical placement is a respect rule, not just a metaphor - a product placed above a Buddha image or royal portrait is offensive
use_for: Compose respect: elders/teachers higher in frame
avoid: Product above sacred items; looming camera over elders in sincere scenes
symbols.evidence_note: Etiquette guides; conceptual-metaphor claim general.

meanings.thai: Freshly made, warmth, care (e.g., morning coffee before shop opens).
meanings.east_asian: Same.

risks_misreadings: Low
use_for: Showing 'fresh / just made / warm welcome' without words
symbols.evidence_note: Index type per Peirce (smoke-fire); reading itself untested.

symbols.symbol: Open shopping bag spilling fresh produce

meanings.thai: Market freshness, home cooking (Thai talad).
meanings.east_asian: Similar.

risks_misreadings: Connotation depends on cultural knowledge (Barthes: 'Italianicity' invisible to Italians)
symbols.evidence_note: Classic semiotic analysis, not tested.

meanings.thai: Eye test, optometrist, 'time to check your eyes'.
meanings.east_asian: Same (letters vary).

risks_misreadings: Using a chart with wrong letters/medical claims may imply clinical service the shop does not offer
use_for: Eye-check reminders, 'how clear is your vision?' hooks
avoid: Claims of diagnosis
symbols.evidence_note: Craft/common knowledge; untested. Links: marketing/ETHICS_AND_THAI_AD_RULES.md (health claims).

meanings.thai: Seeing clearly with right glasses.
meanings.east_asian: Same.

risks_misreadings: Exaggerated 'cure' implication if paired with health claims
use_for: Product clips: before/after clarity as experience, not medical claim
avoid: Implying glasses fix eye disease
symbols.evidence_note: Iconic simulation of experience; untested.

meanings.thai: Caution (international ISO convention).
meanings.east_asian: Same.

risks_misreadings: Pictograms below ~67% comprehension are not safe to stand alone (ISO 3864 criterion as cited by Gungor 2023; ANSI Z535.3 uses 85%)
Real-world mean comprehension of 22 common safety signs was only 66.6% (Gungor 2023)
avoid: Icon-only safety messages
symbols.evidence_note: Standard method (ISO 9186-1 page) + Gungor 2023 Heliyon study read in full; thresholds cited there, standards not read.

symbols.symbol: Visual figure: juxtaposition (two things side by side)

meanings.thai: Works if both objects are familiar to Thai viewers.
meanings.east_asian: Same.

risks_misreadings: Unrelated pairs are processed slowest and liked least
use_for: Glasses beside a matching object (shape rhyme) - easiest metaphor
avoid: Obscure pairings
symbols.evidence_note: Typology + experiments.

symbols.symbol: Visual figure: fusion / hybrid (two objects merged)

meanings.thai: Engaging for followers who stop to look.
meanings.east_asian: Same.

risks_misreadings: Harder to comprehend; complexity lowers liking past a point
avoid: Fast-scroll ads, tourist audiences
symbols.evidence_note: Hybrids preferred in one European study; harder in another - mixed.

meanings.thai: Needs strong context or caption anchorage.
meanings.east_asian: Same.

risks_misreadings: Highest risk of non-comprehension, especially for viewers lacking cultural competency
use_for: Only with a caption that anchors
avoid: Standalone cross-cultural ads
symbols.evidence_note: Complexity ordering from typology; cultural competency effect.

symbols.symbol: Colour symbolism (day colours, black/white mourning, red+gold, saffron, yellow/royal)

meanings.thai: see creative-intelligence/knowledge/visual-arts/ADVANCED_COLOR_SCIENCE.md section 7
meanings.east_asian: see creative-intelligence/knowledge/visual-arts/ADVANCED_COLOR_SCIENCE.md section 7

risks_misreadings: Royal colours and mourning periods are timing-sensitive
symbols.evidence_note: Covered in ADVANCED_COLOR_SCIENCE.md 7.2 - not repeated here.
